quests.instruction: Mira gets home from school with a heavy backpack. Where should it go so nobody trips on it?
quests.correctAnswer: On a hook by the door 🎒
options: On a hook by the door 🎒
In the middle of the hallway 🚶
quests.hint: Pick a spot that is off the floor and easy to find tomorrow morning.
quests.explanation: A bag on a hook or shelf is off the floor and ready to grab. Bags left in hallways or on stairs can make people trip.
quests.funFact: A backpack feels lighter on your shoulders when the heaviest things are packed closest to your back.

quests.instruction: Which of these belongs on a shoe rack?
quests.hint: Think about what might be muddy after a walk.
quests.explanation: Boots and shoes carry dirt, so they stay on a rack near the door, away from clean clothes.
quests.funFact: Putting shoes away in pairs makes it faster to find both of them in the morning.

quests.instruction: Which things are best kept where you can grab them as you leave for school?
quests.hint: Think of the things you need every single morning.
quests.explanation: Things used daily belong near the door, so leaving home is quick and calm. Things used rarely can be stored farther away.
quests.funFact: A launch pad by the door, with room for bags, keys, and shoes, makes mornings smoother.

quests.instruction: Which pair should NOT be stored together?
quests.hint: In one pair, one of the things would make the other one dirty.
quests.explanation: Dirty clothes belong in a laundry basket. Mixing them with clean ones would make everything need washing again.
quests.funFact: Two laundry baskets, one for light colors and one for dark, make washing day simpler.

quests.instruction: Winter coats are not needed in summer. Where could they wait until the cold returns?
quests.correctAnswer: In a box on a high shelf 📦
options: On the floor by the door 🚪
In a box on a high shelf 📦
quests.hint: A good spot is out of the way but still safe.
quests.explanation: Clothes for another season can be stored neatly out of the way, so everyday spaces are not crowded. Clean and dry is best.
quests.funFact: Washing a coat before storing it helps it stay fresh until next winter.

quests.instruction: Maya's drawer is stuffed so full that it will not close. What would help most?
quests.correctAnswer: Take out clothes that no longer fit 👚
options: Take out clothes that no longer fit 👚
Add a few more clothes on top 🧦
quests.hint: A full drawer needs less inside it, not more force.
quests.explanation: Taking out outgrown clothes makes space and makes everyday things easier to find. Forcing a drawer can break it.
quests.funFact: Clothes that are too small can be passed on to a sibling or given to someone who needs them.

quests.instruction: Glasses break easily. Where in the kitchen are they safest?
options: Piled up on the counter edge 🍽️
quests.hint: Choose a spot where they cannot be knocked off or squashed.
quests.explanation: A steady shelf keeps glasses in place and out of the way. Piles at an edge can fall, and stacking them in a pot could crack them.
quests.funFact: In some kitchens glasses are stored upside down so dust does not collect inside.

quests.instruction: How should plates be stacked in the cupboard?
quests.hint: Think about which plate could carry the weight of all the others.
quests.explanation: Big plates are the widest and sturdiest, so they make a steady base for the smaller ones. Tall towers can tip and smash.
quests.funFact: Many kitchens have plate racks that stand the plates on their edges.

quests.instruction: Pots and big mixing bowls are heavy. Where is the safest place to keep them?
quests.hint: Lifting something heavy down from high up is risky.
quests.explanation: Heavy things stored low are easier and safer to lift. A heavy pot falling from up high could hurt someone.
quests.funFact: Most kitchens keep their heaviest pots in the bottom cupboards, near the stove.

quests.instruction: Zeynep's building blocks are spread across the floor. What would make clean-up fastest?
quests.hint: Choose something wide and open that can take many small pieces at once.
quests.explanation: A basket or box lets you scoop up lots of pieces at once, so tidying takes minutes. Racks and bathroom shelves are not made for loose toys.
quests.funFact: Some toy boxes have lids that close slowly, so little fingers do not get pinched.

quests.instruction: Why should toys with tiny pieces be kept away from a baby?
quests.correctAnswer: Babies may put them in their mouths 👶
options: The pieces may get lost in the dust 🧹
The pieces take up too much room 📦
Babies may put them in their mouths 👶
quests.hint: Babies explore the world with their mouths.
quests.explanation: Small parts can block a baby's airway. Toys with tiny pieces are kept in a separate spot, out of a baby's reach.
quests.funFact: Toy makers print age labels on boxes to show which toys are safe for little ones.

quests.instruction: Eli has finished his library book. Where should it go until it is returned?
options: Under the bed with the toys 🛏️
quests.hint: Choose a spot where it will be easy to find on return day.
quests.explanation: Keeping borrowed books together in one place makes them easier to find and return on time.
quests.funFact: Many libraries have a drop slot, so books can be returned even when the library is closed.

quests.instruction: Which pair of foods can wait safely in a cupboard?
quests.hint: Foods with very little moisture keep well without cold.
quests.explanation: Dry foods like rice and pasta keep well at room temperature. Yogurt, cheese, cut fruit, and leftovers need the cold to stay fresh.
quests.funFact: Rice and dry pasta can last for months when kept dry and sealed.

quests.instruction: Which of these should go in the fridge after it has been opened?
quests.hint: A food with plenty of moisture can spoil once air gets in.
quests.explanation: Opened sauce can spoil at room temperature, so it goes in the fridge. Flour and cereal are dry and stay in the cupboard.
quests.funFact: Many jars say 'refrigerate after opening' right on the label.

quests.instruction: A family finds fuzzy green spots on a slice of bread. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up and throw it out 🗑️
options: Pick off the spots and eat it 🍞
Tell a grown-up and throw it out 🗑️
Put it back in the bread bin 🗄️
quests.hint: Mold can spread where you cannot see it.
quests.explanation: Moldy bread should not be eaten, because mold can spread through the whole loaf. An adult can throw it out and wipe the bread box.
quests.funFact: Keeping bread dry and covered helps slow mold down.

quests.instruction: Leo wears his school shoes every day but his party shoes once a year. Where should each pair go?
quests.correctAnswer: School shoes by the door, party shoes in a high box 👟
options: Party shoes by the door, school shoes in a high box 👞
School shoes by the door, party shoes in a high box 👟
Both pairs in a high box 📦
quests.hint: The things you use most should take the least effort to reach.
quests.explanation: Putting daily items in easy spots saves time, and rarely used things can go farther away. Storage works best when it matches how often you use something.
quests.funFact: Organizers call this storing by frequency: the more often you use it, the closer it should be.

quests.instruction: How could a family help a young child get dressed without help?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep everyday clothes in a low drawer 🧦
options: Keep everyday clothes on the highest shelf 📤
Keep everyday clothes in a locked trunk 🧳
Keep everyday clothes in a low drawer 🧦
quests.hint: He can only choose clothes that he can reach.
quests.explanation: A low drawer lets a child pick out and put away clothes alone, which builds independence.
quests.funFact: Children's wardrobes often have rails set low for the same reason.

quests.instruction: Why do spare blankets often go on a top shelf?
options: They are nice to look at 👀
quests.hint: Think about how often you use a spare.
quests.explanation: Spare blankets are not used daily, so the top shelf keeps the easy spots free for things you reach for all the time.
quests.funFact: Spares of almost everything, from light bulbs to blankets, end up on higher or farther shelves.

quests.instruction: Which of these should always be kept where young children cannot reach it?
quests.hint: One of these could be harmful if swallowed or sprayed in the eyes.
quests.explanation: Cleaning products can poison or burn, so adults keep them high up or locked away. Toys and books are made for children to use.
quests.funFact: Many cleaning bottles have child-resistant caps, but they still need to be stored out of reach.

quests.instruction: Why are medicines kept high up or locked away?
quests.correctAnswer: They can harm someone who takes them by mistake 💊
options: They might leak and stain the whole shelf 🧴
They can harm someone who takes them by mistake 💊
They collect dust when left out in the open 🧹
quests.hint: Think about what could happen if someone small swallowed one.
quests.explanation: Medicine is meant for a certain person in a certain amount. Taking it by mistake can be dangerous, so only a grown-up should give it.
quests.funFact: Pharmacy labels say who the medicine is for and how much to take.

quests.instruction: You find a bottle with no label on a low shelf. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Leave it and tell a grown-up 🙋
options: Leave it and tell a grown-up 🙋
Smell it to find out what it is 👃
Pour a little to check the color 🧪
quests.hint: Unknown liquids can be harmful even to smell or touch.
quests.explanation: You cannot tell what is in an unlabeled bottle, and some liquids are dangerous. Leave it alone and get an adult.
quests.funFact: Labels list what is inside and how to use it safely, which is why a bottle without one is a warning sign.

quests.instruction: Dad is tidying a kitchen cupboard. Which item does NOT belong in it?
quests.hint: Look for the thing that belongs on a bed, not at a meal.
quests.explanation: Bowls and tinned food are kitchen items. A pillow belongs in a bedroom, where it stays clean and soft.
quests.funFact: Kitchens are often organized in zones: one for cooking, one for washing up, and one for storing food.

quests.instruction: A bedroom shelf holds a book, a small clock, and one more thing. Which one does not belong?
quests.hint: Work out what would leave dirt behind on a shelf.
quests.explanation: Muddy sports gear belongs by the door or in a storage spot, not on a shelf with books and clocks.
quests.funFact: A shelf with a few chosen things on it is easier to keep tidy than a crowded one.

quests.instruction: A bike helmet, a ball, and a skipping rope are all used outdoors. Where does it make sense to keep them?
quests.correctAnswer: In a basket near the door 🧺
options: In a basket near the door 🧺
In a drawer of spoons and forks 🍴
quests.hint: Pick the spot closest to where they get used.
quests.explanation: Outdoor gear is easiest to grab and put back when it lives near the door. Cutlery drawers and sink cupboards are for other things.
quests.funFact: A basket by the door is a quick home for gear that has nowhere else to go.

quests.instruction: Clean towels should stay dry and fresh. Where should they be kept?
quests.hint: Damp places make towels smell musty.
quests.explanation: Dry spots keep towels clean and fresh. Wet places would make them damp again and smelly.
quests.funFact: Towels dry fastest when they hang with space around them, so air can reach every side.

quests.instruction: Why should the basket of clean, folded laundry be kept apart from the dirty basket?
quests.correctAnswer: So clean clothes do not get dirty again 🧺
options: So the dirty basket stays lighter ⚖️
So the clean clothes dry faster ☀️
So clean clothes do not get dirty again 🧺
quests.hint: Mixing the two baskets would undo your work.
quests.explanation: Keeping clean and dirty clothes apart means the clean ones stay clean and you can see what still needs washing.
quests.funFact: Laundry that is folded right after drying also has fewer wrinkles.

quests.instruction: Where should a toothbrush go after brushing so that it can dry?
options: In a closed drawer while wet 🗄️
quests.hint: Air needs to reach the bristles.
quests.explanation: A toothbrush dries best standing up where air can reach it. Closed drawers and wet sinks keep it damp and dirty.
quests.funFact: Keeping each person's brush in its own spot stops the bristles touching and sharing germs.

quests.instruction: Rana puts crayons, board games, and storybooks into three boxes and labels each one. What is the main benefit?
quests.hint: Labels are a message to everyone in the home.
quests.explanation: Labels tell everyone where things belong, so finding and returning them gets easier for the whole family.
quests.funFact: Labels with little pictures help children who cannot read yet.

quests.instruction: Which habit saves the most time over a whole week?
quests.correctAnswer: Putting things back where they live ↩️
options: Putting things back where they live ↩️
quests.hint: Think about all the minutes spent searching.
quests.explanation: When everything has a home and goes back to it, you spend almost no time searching. Random hiding spots and rare tidying lead to lost things.
quests.funFact: A home for everything makes it easier for the whole family to find things.

quests.instruction: Tom's toys, books, and shoes are all piled together. What is the best first step to organize them?
options: Add more things to the pile ➕
quests.hint: Before putting things away, decide what goes with what.
quests.explanation: Sorting into groups shows what you have and which things belong together. Then each group gets its own home.
quests.funFact: Sorting first is how professional organizers begin, too.
